monument_name: Tarpibaḍā Śikhara Temple 2 (built around the 13th-15th cent.)
description_en: Tarpibaḍā Śikhara Temple 2, built around the 13th-15th centuries, is the smaller of twośikharatemples that face each other and are about 20 meters north of a stone fountain (JUM0443).JUM0441is the larger of the two temples. The three monuments (twośikharatemples and stone fountain) are located on the eastern bank of the Sinja River, opposite the villages of Jacha (to the south-west) and Tarpibaḍā (to the north-west). The temples and the fountain are built on terraces that are currently planted with apple trees. The monuments are described by D. R. Sharma (Sharma 2012: 192-193).The Temple 2 is partially buried and faces west. Its pediment is embellished with carved horizontal friezes, and the doorjambs are also decorated with spirals. The sanctum is empty and has a very reduced inner space that only allows for the deposit of offerings. It could have contained a smallśivaliṅga. The upper part of the Temple appears to have been dismantled and reassembled. Anāmalakadisc is placed on top of the structure. It could be from this monument or from the larger one in front of it.Elements from anotherśikharatemple are scattered around the site. They could have originated from a third temple that stood next to the two existing monuments, or from a separate group.From the 13th to the 15th centuries, suchśikharatemples were built throughout the Karnali Basin (Andolfatto 2019). The rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally known asdevala) complicates dating of these monuments. Two similar temples can be found a few kilometres to the north of the site, above the village of Sanjyalbada (JUM0510), and date from the 13th-15th centuries. The similarity of the two sites' plans suggests that the Tarpibaḍā Temple1 and 2 were also constructed around the same time. This dates to the end of the Khaśa Malla kingdom (12th-14th century) and the reign of the Kalyāl dynasty from Jumla (15th century).
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université. Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
